summary:
GreenRoots is a farm-planning tool developed for the NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge, Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.

It combines satellite observations with soil, weather and crop-history data to show how different parts of a field face different conditions. It checks soil moisture, heat and vegetation patterns, rainfall, erosion risks and nearby crop patterns.

GreenRoots then compares the current crop rotation with three alternative five-year plans. Users can adjust the importance of water conservation, soil health, profitability and forage, and see the trade-offs in a simple dashboard.

It also highlights missing data and areas with lower confidence, helping farmers understand when local checks or expert advice are needed.

The goal is to make satellite information easier to understand and more useful for everyday farming decisions.
details:
How GreenRoots Works

GreenRoots currently supports farms in the continental United States, up to 400 hectares.

Users can select one of two example farms in Iowa and California or draw their own field on the map.

The system combines NASA satellite observations with publicly available soil, weather and crop datasets on a shared 10 m analysis grid. It then divides the field into 3–4 smaller zones based on their characteristics.

For each zone, GreenRoots checks:

  • Soil moisture at different depths.
  • Erosion and bare-soil exposure.
  • Vegetation and heat conditions.
  • Nearby crop patterns and potential pest risks.
  • Data quality, missing information and confidence.

Crop Rotation Planning

GreenRoots compares the existing crop rotation with three alternative five-year plans:

  1. Water & Subsoil Miner: Focuses on water conservation and drought resilience.
  2. Soil-Bank Rebuilder: Focuses on soil health, organic matter and cover crops.
  3. Balanced Cash & Forage: Balances farm income with forage and soil management.

Users can adjust their priorities for water conservation, soil health, profit and forage. The dashboard shows the differences between the plans, including estimated financial and environmental trade-offs.

Technology Used

Backend: Python, FastAPI, GeoPandas, Rasterio, NumPy and Scikit-learn.

Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, MapLibre GL, Terra Draw and Recharts.

Data & AI: NASA Earthdata, Google Earth Engine and Google Gemini API.

What Makes It Different?

Instead of giving one general recommendation for an entire farm, GreenRoots considers the differences between smaller areas of the same field.

It also explains its results, shows confidence levels and highlights missing data rather than presenting every recommendation as certain.

The project is designed to support farmers and agricultural experts, not replace their experience or local field inspections.

The current version is a decision-support prototype. Its financial and environmental outputs are estimates and should be checked against local agricultural knowledge before being used for actual farming decisions.
